title: Caregiver-diary symptoms -> drug classes with labelled adverse effects (older-adult medication review)
purpose: Lets MedWatch say, for a symptom logged in the diary, which of the person's medicines are known (from FDA labelling) to list that symptom as a possible side effect - as a discussion prompt for the clinician/pharmacist, never as a causal claim.

method.summary: For each diary symptom we list drug classes commonly implicated in older adults (class choice guided by AGS Beers 2023, STOPPFall, CDC STEADI and geriatric pharmacology), then check 1-6 representative generics against current FDA Structured Product Labeling via the openFDA drug-label API. Every regex match in the boxed warning, adverse reactions, warnings/precautions, geriatric use and OTC 'when using / stop use / ask a doctor' sections is examined and classified.

hitClassification.termMatch: 'exact' = the symptom's core term (coreTermRegex) appears; 'related' = only a mechanism/near-synonym term (e.g. 'syncope', 'thinking abnormal', 'diuresis', 'accidental injury', 'bronchospasm').
hitClassification.contextFlags: The sentence (or nearby table cells) around a match is checked for contexts that make it weak evidence of an ongoing-use side effect: serotonin syndrome, adrenal insufficiency, hepatotoxicity, overdose, hypersensitivity/angioedema, hyperglycaemia, withdrawal/discontinuation, pancreatitis, NMS, MAOI interaction, paediatric-only statements, interaction-only statements, lactic acidosis, alcohol reactions. Flagged matches are never counted as evidence; for each drug the best clean hit per section is kept (max 3).
hitClassification.geriatricUseLabelMention: Generics whose label mentions the symptom in its Geriatric Use subsection (8.5) - direct older-adult labelling evidence.
hitClassification.labelEvidenceLevel: Per class: 'exact' if any representative drug has a clean exact hit; 'related' if only clean related-term hits; 'none' otherwise.

method.labelSelection: openFDA search on openfda.generic_name, preferring single-ingredient human prescription labels with an adverse-reactions section, then the most recent effective date. Labels are often generic manufacturers' SPLs; brand labels may differ slightly. Each hit stores SPL set id, DailyMed link, effective date, section, matched term and a snippet so a reviewer can check it.
method.fallback: If no exact label hit, NLM MedlinePlus consumer drug information (resolved via MedlinePlus Connect from the RxNorm RxCUI) is searched with the same rules and stored as medlineplusEvidence.
limitations: A label listing an adverse reaction does not mean the drug caused a given person's symptom; trial frequencies and placebo rates are not captured as structured data (they are often visible in the snippet).
Representative drugs stand in for classes; individual agents differ (e.g. peripheral oedema is mostly a dihydropyridine-CCB effect; verapamil is the CCB most associated with constipation).
Older-adult specificity comes from the class choice (Beers/STOPPFall/STEADI) and crossLinks, not from the labels, which describe the general adult population.
Regex classification can still miss negated statements (e.g. 'no increase in X'); snippets are stored for human review.
Labels rarely use the word 'fall'; frids.json is the authority for falls.
method.snomed: Codes verified with tx.fhir.org CodeSystem/$lookup against SNOMED CT International Edition 20250201 (all active on 2026-10-10). display = preferred term; fsn = fully specified name. Production use of SNOMED CT requires a licence (free in IHTSDO member countries such as the US via the NLM UMLS licence).

fhirHint.note: Use Observation.effectiveDateTime for the diary day; keep the free-text utterance in Observation.note; link a suspected medicine with Observation.focus or a separate AdverseEvent only after clinician review.

engineGuidance.language: Say 'X is listed on its FDA label as a possible cause of <symptom> (source)'. Never say X caused the symptom. Combine with timing from the diary (e.g. 'dizziness was logged on 9 of 14 days after X was started; 2 of 14 before').
engineGuidance.ranking: Rank classes for a logged symptom by: labelEvidenceLevel exact > related > none-with-guideline/MedlinePlus; then whether the person's drug is a Beers PIM / FRID / ACB >= 2 (crossLinks); then recency of start or dose change.
engineGuidance.matching: Match the person's medicines to classes by ingredient (RxNorm RxCUI or generic); representativeGenerics are examples, not the full class.
